title: Repaso de B1: used to y would para hábitos del pasado

rule.title: Past habits: used to and would
rule.explanation:
El examen de B2 vuelve a preguntar cómo hablar de hábitos del pasado.

«Used to» + verbo sirve para hábitos y estados del pasado que ya no son así. En negativa y pregunta, «use to» sin d:
- «I used to live in Madrid.»
- «I didn't use to like coffee.»
- «Did you use to play an instrument?»

«Would» + verbo sirve solo para acciones repetidas, sobre todo al contar recuerdos; no para estados:
- «Every summer my grandad would take me fishing.»
- «I used to have long hair.» (estado: nunca «I would have long hair» con este sentido)

Para una sola vez, el past simple: «I moved to Bristol in 2023».

No los confundas con «be used to» / «get used to» + «-ing» (estar acostumbrado / acostumbrarse):
- «I'm used to working late.»
- «I'm getting used to the weather.»

sets.instructions: Completa con «used to», «use to», «would» o la forma correcta.

items.sentence: When I was a student, I ___ share a flat with five people.
Did you ___ have a pet when you were a child?
Every Sunday my grandmother ___ make a huge lunch.
I ___ be very shy, but now I love speaking in public.
We didn't ___ have a car, so we walked everywhere.
After school we ___ play football until it got dark.
She ___ live in Paris before she moved to London.
I ___ to Bristol in 2023. (move, una sola vez)
I'm used to ___ late. It's normal in my job. (work)
It took me a year to get used ___ driving on the left.
There ___ to be a cinema on this street.
My dad ___ read to us every night before bed.
